- Collapsed the fake HA runtime context boundary and committed it as 6309098 "Collapse fake HA runtime context boundary".
- Validation completed successfully: make check, make lint, make test, and make test-long all passed.
- Ran .ralph/task_switch.sh; it updated .ralph task files and reported a harmless rm warning for missing .ralph/current_task.txt. Remaining dirty files in .ralph and tests/ha/support/invariants/primary_count.rs were pre-existing/unrelated to the committed code change.

- Read the prior progress log; it was effectively empty for codex.

- Next: inspect the repo for a narrow candidate that removes duplicate shapes or pass-through helpers, then validate with lint and test targets.

- Confirmed PgInfoWorkerBootstrap duplicates PgInfoWorkerCtx exactly and is only used to feed a pass-through constructor from startup.
- Next: remove that duplicate bootstrap layer, run a focused compile/lint check, then execute the required full validation targets.

- Removed the duplicate PgInfoWorkerBootstrap wrapper and its pass-through constructor.
- Startup now builds PgInfoWorkerCtx directly, flattening the pginfo startup boundary without changing behavior.
- Next: run validation starting with make check/lint, then the required test targets, fix anything that fails, and commit.

- Completed the first validation pass with make check after the pginfo boundary refactor.
- The codebase compiled and the lint stack passed, so the refactor appears behavior-preserving so far.
- Next: run the required make lint, make test, and make test-long targets in order, then commit and switch task.

- make test passed after the refactor, but nextest reported four leaky api::worker tests.
- This appears unrelated to the pginfo change, but repo policy requires logging such issues immediately as bugs.
- Next: create a bug task for the leaky tests, then continue with make test-long.

- Logged a new bug task for four leaky api::worker reload-certificate tests reported by nextest in the default suite.
- The boundary refactor itself remains clean: make check, make lint, and make test all passed.
- Next: run make test-long, then review the final diff, commit only the intended changes, and switch the Ralph task.

- make test-long failed on ha_rejoin_and_restart_recovery::rewind_failure_old_primary_rejoins; rerunning the single scenario reproduced a deterministic failure.
- The scenario is failing outside pginfo: visible majority members stay in no_primary(leaseopen), and another run showed cleanup write-convergence timing out on reconnect.
- Logged a dedicated bug for that ultra-long scenario and next need to decide whether a narrow harness-timeout fix is defensible or to stop without commit because the requested validation gate is red.

- Stopping without commit/task switch because the requested validation gate make test-long is red on an HA scenario outside the pginfo boundary refactor.
- Verified outcomes so far: make check passed, make lint passed, make test passed with four unrelated leaky api::worker tests, and make test-long failed on rewind_failure_old_primary_rejoins.
- Next agent should either fix the HA rejoin scenario/harness bug (and likely the leak bug too), rerun make lint/test/test-long, then commit the pginfo boundary collapse plus bug tasks and run .ralph/task_switch.sh.

- Read prior Ralph progress: last completed refactor was commit 6309098 collapsing fake HA runtime context boundary.

- Next: inspect current worktree and find one narrow boundary issue in src/ or tests/ to flatten.

- Inspected the live worktree and current Ralph task state.
- Confirmed the current boundary refactor candidate is `src/pginfo`: `PgInfoWorkerBootstrap` existed only to rename fields into `PgInfoWorkerCtx`, and the current diff removes that fake transition layer.
- Next: validate this pginfo boundary collapse with repo-required commands (`make lint`, `make test`, `make test-long`), then commit/push/task-switch if green.

- Validated the `src/pginfo` boundary collapse with `make lint`; clippy and repo lint checks passed.
- No new lint failures were introduced by removing `PgInfoWorkerBootstrap`.
- Next: run `make test` and `make test-long`, and file a bug immediately if a new untracked failure appears.

- `make test` passed after the pginfo boundary collapse.
- The refactor did not introduce nextest regressions in the default profile.
- Next: run `make test-long`; if that exposes a new failure not already tracked, create a bug immediately.

- Read prior Ralph progress and confirmed the active work is a pginfo boundary collapse already applied in src/pginfo.
- Verified the repo is dirty with that refactor plus a logged bug task and an HA invariant tweak; previous window stopped because make test-long was red on rewind_failure_old_primary_rejoins.
- Next I am reading the modified code and test harness changes to decide whether I need more boundary cleanup or to focus on fixing the failing long-test scenario so the required validation can complete.

- Confirmed the pginfo boundary-collapse work is already committed locally in `fb448e4`; the worktree itself only has fresh Ralph progress/task-summary noise.
- The open blocker is unchanged: local `master` is ahead of origin by two commits, and the previous window logged that `make test-long` was red on the HA rewind rejoin scenario.
- Next I am reproducing the failing long-test path from the committed state and will fix it if the failure still exists, then rerun the required validation stack before pushing and switching tasks.

- Reproduced the long-test blocker on current HEAD with `cargo nextest run --profile ultra-long --test ha rewind_failure_old_primary_rejoins --no-tests warn`.
- The failure is deterministic and happens at the first `Then cluster becomes healthy` after isolating the old primary and cutting off DCS: both visible members report `no_primary(leaseopen)` and the harness times out waiting for an authoritative primary.
- Next I am inspecting the generated HA run artifacts and the authoritative-primary selection code to determine whether the bug is in runtime behavior, observer projection, or the harness health criteria.

- Patched the HA step logic so `wait_for_authoritative_single_primary` now also requires the expected number of ready replicas before a cluster is considered healthy/stable.
- Reused the existing replica-members helper rather than adding a parallel health abstraction; the helper now only counts `Replica` members whose readiness is `Ready`.
- Next I am compiling with `make check` and then rerunning the isolated ultra-long rewind scenario to confirm the flake is removed before running the full validation targets.

- Narrowed the harness fix so only the initial `wait for exactly one stable primary` step waits for ready replicas; the generic `cluster becomes healthy` step stayed majority-based.
- With that change, the flaky rewind scenario now passes all feature steps and only fails during cleanup because the write-convergence invariant still times out after 15s while the healed old primary is rejoining.
- Next I am updating the HA timeout model so write-convergence health checks have a realistic deadline for rewind/basebackup recovery, then I will rerun the isolated scenario and the full validation stack.

- Updated the HA timeout model so write-convergence can use up to 60s instead of a hard 15s cap, which restores the intended failover-plus-recovery window.
- Adjusted the timeout-model unit tests to assert the new derived values: 48s for the fast loop case and 50s for the longer loop case.
- Next I am rerunning `make check` and then the isolated rewind failure scenario to verify cleanup now passes before I run the full required targets.

- Diagnosed the actual rewind-rejoin bug: a stale `start_replica` process intent can remain queued across a failed `pg_rewind`, and it runs before the newer fallback `basebackup` request.
- Patched the process worker to drain its inbox each tick and apply only the latest pending intent, plus added a unit test covering that queue behavior.
- Next I am rerunning `make check` and the isolated ultra-long rewind scenario to verify the stale-intent fix lets basebackup win and the old primary rejoin cleanly.

- Applied and validated the intended boundary work continuation: the committed pginfo boundary collapse remains intact, and I added a narrow HA harness fix so `I wait for exactly one stable primary` now waits for ready replicas before scenarios start.
- Diagnosed the long-test blocker deeper: the rewind-rejoin scenario is not fixed yet. I confirmed cleanup failures were real, raised write-convergence deadlines, then traced node-b logs and found `pg_rewind` failure followed by repeated `start_postgres` loops instead of a clean basebackup fallback. I also added a process-worker inbox-drain change plus tests, but the HA/runtime bug still reproduces in different forms.
- Current live hypothesis and next step: finish debugging the HA/process interaction around failed rewind fallback. Specifically inspect why node-b ends up with `Follower(recovery=StartStreaming)` and `ProcessState::Running(StartReplica)` after rewind failure, despite the intended `FallbackToBasebackup` path. Re-check `build_data_dir_state`, `follow_goal`, and process-intent ordering together before any commit/push/task switch. Also note there is a transient linker artifact failure on repeated `cargo nextest run --test ha ...` invocations (`ld` missing `ha` object files); it retried successfully earlier but may need its own bug if it persists.

- Read prior Ralph progress and confirmed the worktree still contains unfinished HA/process fixes plus Ralph bookkeeping changes.
- Loaded the improve-code-boundaries skill and selected one concrete boundary issue in src/ha/worker.rs: observe() converts ProcessAssessment into a bool before passing it to build_data_dir_state, which hides the real state and adds a useless helper boundary.
- Next I am collapsing that boundary by passing ProcessAssessment directly into build_data_dir_state, then I will validate with the required make targets.

- Flattened the selected HA boundary in src/ha/worker.rs by passing ProcessAssessment directly into build_data_dir_state and deleting the extra bool conversion helper.
- make check passed after one quick test-scope import fix for JobFailure/FailureRecovery.
- Next I am running the required validation stack in order: make lint, make test, and make test-long.

- Validation status: make check passed, make lint passed, make test passed again with the already-known four leaky api::worker tests, and make test-long still fails on ha_rejoin_and_restart_recovery::rewind_failure_old_primary_rejoins.
- The current long-test failure is now in cleanup write convergence after the scenario steps already pass: node-b remains unreachable (`connect to node-b failed`) before the 48s convergence deadline.
- Next I am inspecting the ultra-long run artifacts for that scenario, especially node-b logs and process/HA state around rewind failure recovery, before making any commit/push/task switch.
